In natural language processing (NLP), a variety of tasks have been addressed regarding explainability of neural networks, such as textual entailment , sentiment classification , machine translation  and question answering . In this paper, we address question answering (QA) due to its proximity to users in real-life settings, for instance, in the context of personal assistants.

Current evaluation of XQA is focused on three scores: (i) answer-F 1 , which is based on the token overlap between the predicted and the ground truth answer, (ii) SP-F 1 , which calculates F 1 based on the overlap of predicted and ground truth relevant ("supporting") facts and (iii) joint-F 1 , which is based on the definitions of joint precision and joint recall as the products of answer and SP precision and recall as described in .
To investigate the relation between different evaluation scores and user experience, we conduct a user study.
